hard: Aina and Danish went to Taman Safari with their class on Sunday.
They rode in a yellow bus and the trip began at 10 am.
Aina wore a white scarf and Danish carried a blue bag.
A ranger called Mrs Rose met the class at the gate.
She gave each child a map of the park.
The children were happy and the day was warm.
The first stop was a wide field of tall gold grass.
A pride of 7 lions lay under a big tree.
A lion can sleep for up to 20 hours each day.
Danish saw a male lion with a thick mane.
He did not wake up, but his tail moved.
Aina took a photo of the pride.
Mrs Rose told the children to stay quiet and calm.
Next the bus drove to a muddy pool.
A tiger sat by the water with 2 cubs.
Every tiger has its own pattern of stripes.
Aina could see orange fur and black stripes.
A tiger can swim, so it likes to cool off in the water.
The mother tiger did not come near the bus, but she watched it closely.
Then the bus passed a forest of tall green trees.
A big gorilla sat in the grass and ate leaves.
Gorillas eat leaves, stems and fruit.
A male gorilla can weigh 200 kg.
A gorilla lives in a family group, so it is never alone.
Danish counted 4 gorillas in the group.
He took a photo of the biggest one.
The last stop was a tall tree full of birds.
A red parrot sat on a branch.
A parrot can copy words from people.
Aina said hello, and the parrot said hello back.
A green parrot sat next to it and did not make a sound.
Danish counted 9 parrots in the tree.
The bus returned to the gate at 3 pm.
Aina and Danish thanked Mrs Rose for the lovely day.
The class waved goodbye to the animals.
It was a great day at the park.
